name.description: studio name, shown in the rail and project list

template.description: mark this project as a studio template: opening it offers "new project from this studio" instead of editing it in place

theme.description: How the studio looks. Parameterized, not raw CSS: an accent re-tints the whole UI coherently (buttons, focus rings, highlights), so every studio stays recognizably Fabulist. Looks only — never trust-gated, and fabulist.local.json may override it.

accent.description: named accent color the UI derives its whole accent ramp from

glyph.description: 1–2 characters/emoji shown as the studio's mark in the rail and project list

docFont.description: default document typeface for prose files; the app chrome keeps its own faces

fileTypes.description: Typed kinds of files this studio works with, matched by filename glob. A matching file gets the icon and label in the rail, its title derived per titleFrom, and a card in the New File dialog (the filename follows the glob, the template seeds the content). Any file kind can be typed (.md, .html, .json, .py, …) — every textual file and image is already a work file; a file type adds meaning on top.

match.description: project-relative filename glob; * and ? stay within one path segment, ** spans folders

label.description: display label; defaults to the id

icon.description: 1–2 characters/emoji shown in the file rail

template.description: seed content for new files of this type; {{title}} is substituted

color.description: named accent tinting this type's glyph in the rail and tab strip

font.description: document typeface for files of this type; overrides theme.docFont

width.description: prose measure for files of this type: "narrow" (58ch), "normal" (74ch, default), "wide" (96ch)

wordCount.description: show a live word count while editing files of this type

fields.description: frontmatter keys edited as a form above the prose: "key" is free text, "key: a | b" a select

actions.description: Commands surfaced in the ⌘K palette (and, for surface "selection", in the highlight toolbar). An action runs a .claude/skills skill, sends a canned prompt, or both.

id.description: stable identifier; defaults to a slug of the label

label.description: palette label (required unless a skill names it)

surface.description: what the action operates on; "selection" needs highlighted text

prompt.description: instructions sent to the project agent (alongside or instead of the skill)

panels.description: Read-only rendered views over project files, opened as ▦ tabs from the rail or palette.

id.description: stable identifier; defaults to a slug of the title

view.description: how the source is rendered: "markdown" (default) renders prose, "code" shows syntax-highlighted source, "image" displays a picture file, "web" embeds the file as a live page (relative assets and scripts work)

commands.description: Shell commands the studio can run at the project root (dev server, build, tests…), started only by the user from the rail — never by the agent — with the exact command line always shown. Output streams into a log tab; a long-running command keeps a ● running indicator until stopped.

id.description: stable identifier; defaults to a slug of the label

label.description: rail label (required unless id is given)

run.description: the shell command line, run at the project root

preview.description: a localhost URL embedded as a live preview beside the log while the command runs

permissions.description: Gate profile; loosening grants requires user trust in the app.

edits.description: "auto" applies the agent's file edits without per-edit approval; only takes effect after the user explicitly trusts the studio in the app

bash.description: "deny" removes the shell tool from the agent entirely (tightening never needs trust)

mcp.description: project MCP servers (.mcp.json + .claude/settings.json enablement): "none" (default) ignores them, "ask" connects them with per-tool approval, "allow" connects and auto-approves their tools; anything but "none" requires the user to trust the studio
